correctness.rationale: The defined 11-vertex 18-edge bipartite graph is the Herschel graph. An independent exhaustive DFS of every simple spanning path, plus a separate Held–Karp recurrence in the inspected proof, shows 444 oriented and 222 undirected Hamiltonian paths; their edge subsets yield exactly 37454 nonempty simplices and f-vector [18,153,796,2742,6402,9913,9738,5694,1776,222]. An independently reconstructed specified vertex-toggle matching has exactly 18724 matched pairs and one 0-cell plus five 6-cells unmatched; a complete topological sort of all 237072 reversed Hasse incidences confirms global acyclicity, not just a Betti count. Forman therefore gives the integral wedge ∨5S6. The degree-defined graph automorphism group is S3×C2. Exact signed fixed-simplex Lefschetz summation over all twelve transformations gives H6 rational character (5,−1,−1,1,−1,1) for S3 classes identity, transposition, three-cycle, each with or without central involution, equal to (sgn⊕Std)⊗1 ⊕Std⊗ε. Averaged character is zero, so no invariants.
residual_risks: Finite independent checks do not prove the all-parameter claims; analytic arguments or exhaustive certificates are required.

value.rationale: Hamiltonian spanning-path containment is a naturally defined simplicial complex on the smallest famous non-Hamiltonian polyhedral graph. Its exact integral homotopy type, unusually concentrated despite pure dimension nine, and the full finite automorphism representation are independently motivated invariants, not an arbitrary tiny parameter substitution. The complete finite exhaustive certificate makes this self-contained.
